privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: No analytics, no ad networks, no tracking cookies, no fingerprinting.
privacy.intro: ZecHub is an open-source education hub for a privacy-preserving currency, so we hold the site itself to the same standard. This page describes, plainly, who can observe that you visited.
privacy.s1b: There are no analytics, no advertising, no tracking cookies, no fingerprinting, and no third-party trackers on this site. Reading the wiki requires no account, and we build no profile of you. We do not opt you into browser ad-topics APIs (they are disabled site-wide).
privacy.s2b: The site is served by our hosting provider (Vercel), which, like any web host, processes the network requests needed to deliver each page and keeps short-lived operational logs. Connections are HTTPS-only (enforced via HSTS). When you click a link that leaves the site, your browser sends only the originating site, never the specific page you were on.
privacy.s3b: Fonts and the brand images on this workspace are hosted here. Article images and wallet logos load from zechub.wiki. Rendering a page therefore makes a request to zechub.wiki for those assets. The original site also uses a small number of Wikimedia logos and live status badges from shields.io.
privacy.s4b: Some articles embed YouTube videos. The embed loads when you open the article, which creates a direct connection to YouTube. YouTube operates under its own privacy policy. The original ZecHub site uses a click-to-load placeholder for these embeds. This workspace does not.
privacy.s5b: This workspace does not include the ZecHub newsletter, wallet likes, or the AI assistant. It has no accounts and no write actions. The wallet ratings and page content are a snapshot. Live network data comes from the public ZecHub APIs.
privacy.s6b: This workspace is public. You can read and audit the code in the repository, and you can read the original privacy statement on zechub.wiki. This page describes the workspace as it currently behaves.

hackathon.rulesTitle: Keep it fair and easy to judge.
hackathon.t1c: Nodes, indexers, RPC tooling, and reliability for builders and operators.
hackathon.t2c: Interactive experiences and game loops where Zcash is part of the fun.
hackathon.t3c: Threshold signing, custody patterns, and safer key management on Zcash.
hackathon.t4c: Auth and identity flows that use Zcash primitives for sign-in or access.
hackathon.t5c: Reporting, reconciliation, and workflows for teams handling ZEC.
hackathon.r1: Projects must interact with the Zcash network in a meaningful way.
hackathon.r2: Teams can submit only one final project per team.
hackathon.r3: All submissions must include clear setup and usage documentation.
hackathon.r4: Use open-source licensing whenever possible to encourage collaboration.
hackathon.r5: Respect privacy, security, and community guidelines in both code and content.
